content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to configure hardware module [article_no] with display [product_name] so that, for instance, key F1 displays three lines of information representing different safety devices, allowing the user to selectively disable any of these via cursor keys? Thank you.

No, that's not possible. You can't dynamically change the context of a text block during operation on [product_name]. You can create two text blocks that are nearly identical except for one line; with an F button on the display, you can activate or deactivate the preferred text block to achieve a similar effect.

Sorry for any confusion. What I'm aiming for is to disable only the function linked to a particular message line, while keeping the text unchanged and retaining the ability to enable the function again as needed.

Hello [user_name], It depends on how your setup is programmed. To show a message text, the 'enable' signal must be true. If several message texts are used, the one with the highest defined priority is shown first. In block properties, the ON/OFF button lets you determine which text appears based on the status of the related function block. Refer to the attached screenshot for more details. Hope this helps with your solution. Greetings, [user_name]
Hello [user_name], With [product_name] [article_no], only digital inputs and outputs can be specified for this function.

[article_no], you're correct—I missed the detail about [article_no] earlier. Nevertheless, [user_name] could use a digital output connected to the desired constant or function block for displaying specific text in the program. Greetings, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are evaluating interactive customization of message texts on [company_name] hardware using [product_name]. The discussion uncovers several restrictions: on-the-fly editing of text blocks is not supported, and only digital inputs/outputs are assignable for enabling or disabling messages. Solutions are limited by available block properties, affecting flexibility in dynamic function control via the operator panel display.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to manage underlying functional states corresponding to message list items directly from the display, with the messages remaining visible and easy toggling of functions using hardware panel keys.
